result.title: Don't Pick a Winner: Knowledge Conflicts Need a Prior, Not a Rule
result.comment: 49 pages (9 main text + appendix and supplementary material), 14 figures
result.summary: A retrieval-augmented language model answers from two sources, the retrieved context and its own knowledge, and the two disagree whenever the context is incomplete or wrong. Existing methods settle the disagreement with a rule fixed at design time: follow the context, amplify it in proportion to how far it moves the model, or trust the model's memory. Each rule is confidently wrong in some deployment. In a decision-theoretic model of two sources, the score of any fixed rule is linear in the share of reliable contexts while the best attainable score is convex, so every fixed rule is beaten wherever it is not exactly optimal; and a symmetric divergence between the two sources, the signal adaptive decoding uses, carries no information about which one is right. Resolving a conflict therefore needs two inputs that no existing method keeps: evidence about each source separately, and a prior on how often the context is right. We test these claims on GRACE, a benchmark that intervenes on the knowledge-graph context of a fixed question, so that what the model knows, what the context says and what is true are measured separately. There, every baseline from four families is strong on right contexts or on wrong ones, never on both. We then build the two inputs: the model states its knowledge as notes, a small policy voices each note with a calibrated confidence, a reader answers in two voices, and a selector commits or abstains under a prior $π$ applied as an exact prior shift. With $π$ set to the true share of right contexts, the system is above the best baseline at every mixture of GRACE contexts, by up to 26 points. Its overall score is 45.3 and 35.0 (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Llama-3.1-8B), against 29.4 and 27.5 for the best baseline. On preregistered ClashEval it beats same-backbone CK-PLUG and TCR by 12 and 26 points. Where the model lacks the knowledge, the gains vanish, as the theory predicts.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究检索增强模型在「检索上下文」与「自身知识」冲突时如何取舍，用决策论说明任何固定规则都只在部分情形最优，并构建分别刻画各来源证据与上下文正确率先验、允许弃权的选择系统，在 GRACE 等基准上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「对称散度不携带哪一来源正确的信息」的论断可供核查以有/无视觉输入输出差异度量视觉依赖的做法；按来源分别建模证据并施加先验、可弃权的选择机制，可能启发视觉证据与语言先验冲突时的取舍与停止决策设计。
